rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different). The 2024 rules' own names keep it too: Fey Ancestry, Fey Touched, Fey Wanderer, Summon Fey and the SRD's Conjure Fey (Chat, 15 November). So does a list of creature types: "any Undead, Fey, or Elemental".
rules.renames_because: The setting's own names for those planes, the first two of the Revelator's Cosmography: the Feywild is the Hidden, the Shadowfell the Ghostlands (setting/whats-out.md, wheel-and-plenum.md). The SRD's "the Feywild" reads "the Hidden".

opening: Euphonia is a fantasy roleplaying setting for the 2024 fifth-edition rules: our own world in the year 1668, where magic is real, history keeps its shape, and the African empire of Mutapa never fell.

In the year 1668, the world has never been more open. The Ottomans, the crowned heads of Europe, Qing China and the rising empire of Mutapa vie with each other for dominance and victory in the great game of politics. A bloody war of resources in South America is about to explode across the continent, as the nations of North America keep a wary eye on the European colonies along their Atlantic shore.

The winds of change are blowing full-force. The old hierarchies of magic and faith have been challenged by natural philosophers and thinkers who don't bother with spells. The Wild Hunt of all peoples beats at the frontiers, raiding and stealing people for unknown purposes. Buried underneath the new neighborhoods of booming cities are old tombs, catacombs filled with threats and the promise of the lost treasures of a thousand ancient empires. Wealth beyond imagining could be yours, as could the ruin of nations.
world: Euphonia starts in Europe, but it doesn't end there. Western Europe is the default theme of most fantasy settings, but Euphonia is designed to be built out globally. Ships traverse every part of the ocean, magic can bridge continents and the world is far more interconnected than before. A dungeon delve can happen in a Mesopotamian ruin, beneath Great Zimbabwe, in the Haudenosaunee woods a French priest calls wilderness, at Angkor Wat and anywhere else in the world. History is rich with inspiration, usually far more interesting than one would even think to fictionalize. Finding adventure anywhere on the planet is the goal.
pitch: You are an exceptional person in a dynamic and changing world. A counsellor in the royal courts of Europe. An artificer plying their trade on the Monsoon Road on the Indian Ocean. A practitioner of healing magics in the halls of Constantinople. A weary Andean priest repelling a mercenary and Spanish raid on your home. A New England experimenter trying not to blow up his home (again). A hunter fighting sea monsters in the South Pacific. A disgraced alchemist breaking into a tomb in Beijing.

Your talents, be they martial, magical or mental, set you apart and make you coveted by any number of powers and factions. Most adventurers end up bossing kings around. What if you work for those kings? What if you're opposed to them? Will you work for the common good? Will you try and walk the halls of power? Are you in it for the money? Or are there darker forces at work through you? Whatever your motivation, you are a power in a world at the crossroads of everything. What will you do with your power?
data.building: **Building on Euphonia.** What the books only sketch is open for anyone to build on. The brief for developers is Appendix F: Building on Euphonia, and what each chapter leaves open is Open for Developers, the last chapter of this book. While the books are in draft, text in square brackets is first-draft flavor that anyone may keep or rewrite.

moment.text: **The lamp in the kitchen.** In Mutapa a lamp that lights itself is a household thing. In Vienna it's a duchess's toy, until she tires of it and it goes downstairs: Regina Mayrhofer, cook to a countess on the Herrengasse, works late under one now and swears by it. It dims a little every month, and the polite foreign tinker who comes to set it right asks a great many friendly questions about the house. What the ministries have just worked out about that lamp is the Mark of 1668, and what the tinker does with his questions is in Characters (Backgrounds, Mutapan Agent).
